title: Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\{b_i:i\in I\}$ is a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$, with a constant-one basis vector, and is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For a natural number $n$, a real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, and a multi-index $a$ of length $n$ with values in $I$, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ is its expectation under the product probability measure $\pi^n$ of $f(x)\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}b_{a(j)}(x(j))$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function basis indexed by $I$
The basis has a constant-one vector
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
A multi-index $a$ of length $n$ with values in $I$
